question.text: A first-time fund manager (Ms. Divya Kapoor, Kosi Ventures) is asked how she will give LPs comfort on 'alignment of interest'. Per Ch 12, the primary mechanism is:

answer.text: Publishing detailed daily NAVs to all LPs.
Committing only the SEBI-minimum continuing interest (2.5% or INR 5 crore, whichever is lower) — since more would be imprudent.
Investing MORE than the mandatory minimum 'continuing interest' to provide greater 'skin-in-the-game' and signal commitment, since many first-time managers do exactly this.
Charging a higher management fee to cover first-time-manager risk.

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 12 — continuing interest provides 'skin-in-the-game' and removes mis-alignment/moral hazard. 'Many first-time managers would invest more than the mandatory minimum continuing interest to provide greater comfort to investors.' The Trap: A is transparency, not alignment. B is minimal-compliance approach — poor signalling. D is opposite — higher fees hurt alignment. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-refers to SEBI (AIF) Reg 10(d) on continuing interest — Cat I/II: 2.5% or INR 5 cr (lower); Cat III: 5% or INR 10 cr (lower).
